concepts.title: Aggregate Built-ins: sum, min and max
concepts.definition: Three ready-made functions read a numeric list in one call: sum() totals the elements, min() returns the smallest and max() the largest, without disturbing the list itself.
concepts.key_idea: For the list [34, 12, 63, 39, 92, 44] the three calls answer 284, 12 and 92.
concepts.textbook_ref: kecs109.txt, section 9.4, Table 9.1 (min, max, sum rows)
question_patterns: For list1 = [34, 12, 63, 39, 92, 44], what do sum(list1), min(list1) and max(list1) return?
Write a function that returns the largest element of the list passed as a parameter.
A list of six prices totals 284 with a smallest entry of 12. What range do the values span from smallest to largest?
Why do sum(), min() and max() leave the original list unchanged?
Find the sum of [52, 8, 4, 2] and state which built-in you used.

solution_steps.explain: Fold the leading elements into a partial sum.
Appending the last two completes the total.

worked_examples.q: For the list [34, 12, 63], what does sum() return?

concepts.title: Average Marks with a Function
concepts.definition: The function computeAverage(list1, n) walks the collected marks, folds each into a running total, and divides by the number of students to produce the class average.
concepts.key_idea: The list is built with append() inside an input loop before the averaging function ever runs.
question_patterns: Marks 45, 89, 79, 76 and 55 are entered for 5 students. What average does computeAverage print?
Write a program that reads n marks into a list and reports the average using a function.
Why must the count n be passed to the function along with the list?
A class of 4 students scores 70, 65, 80 and 85. Compute the average marks.
What happens to the average if one student's marks are appended twice by mistake?

solution_steps.explain: Each of the five marks joins the running total.
solution_steps.compute: total = m1 + m2 + m3 + m4 + m5

solution_steps.explain: The average spreads the total over n students.

worked_examples.q: Six students' marks total 420. What average does computeAverage report?

concepts.title: Append versus Extend
concepts.definition: append() drops its whole argument in as one single new element, even when the argument is itself a list, while extend() unwraps the argument list and attaches each element separately, so the two calls grow a list by different amounts.
concepts.key_idea: Appending [50, 60] adds one nested element; extending with [80, 90] adds two flat elements.
question_patterns: Starting from myList = [10, 20, 30, 40], what does myList look like after append([50, 60]) and then extend([80, 90])?
How many elements does myList hold after both operations of the previous question?
Why does append([50, 60]) create a nested element rather than two new numbers?
Which call would you use to merge a second list into the first, and why?
What error appears when a list is concatenated with a plain string using +?

solution_steps.explain: One nested element joins, whatever its inner size.
Each element of the argument list joins separately.

worked_examples.q: list1 holds 3 elements. After list1.extend([80, 90]), how many elements does it hold?

concepts.title: Negative Step Slicing of Lists
concepts.definition: Slicing works on lists exactly as on strings: list1[n:m] copies positions n up to m minus 1, and a negative step walks from the end backwards, so list1[::-1] hands back the whole list reversed and list1[::-2] keeps every second element from the right.
concepts.key_idea: A first index larger than the second yields an empty list, and a runaway second index shrinks to the list end.
question_patterns: How many elements does list1[::-2] select from the list [1, 2, ..., 10], and which ones?
For the colour list of section 9.2.4, what do list1[2:6] and list1[-6:-2] return?
Why does list1[7:2] evaluate to an empty list?
Predict the output of list1[0:6:2] on the seven-element colour list.
What single slice expression reverses a list without creating an explicit loop?

solution_steps.explain: With both ends defaulted the span equals the list size.
Round the absolute span up over the step size.

worked_examples.q: What list does list1[::-1] return for the list [1, 2, 3]?

concepts.title: Linear Search Position
concepts.definition: The function linearSearch(num, list1) compares the target with each element from the front; on a match it returns the zero-based index, which the caller converts to a human-friendly position by adding one, and it returns None when nothing matches.
concepts.key_idea: A target at index i costs i comparisons on elements before it, and the i plus oneth comparison finds it.
question_patterns: In the list 23, 567, 12, 89, 324, at which position is 12 found by linear search?
Write a function that returns the position of a number in a list, or a suitable message when absent.
How many comparisons does linear search make before locating the element at index 2?
Why does Program 9-5 print result + 1 rather than result itself?
What does linearSearch return when the number never appears, and how does the caller detect it?

solution_steps.action: count the elements before the hit
solution_steps.explain: Each earlier element costs one failed comparison.
Adding one turns the zero-based index into the printed position.

worked_examples.q: Linear search finds 30 at zero-based index 4. What human-friendly position does the caller report?

concepts.title: Nested List Student Record
concepts.definition: A record such as ['Raman', 'A-36', [56, 98, 99, 72, 69], 78.8] nests the five subject marks inside a list, so two indices reach a single mark as stRecord[2][j], and dividing the inner total by five rebuilds the stored percentage.
concepts.key_idea: The first index picks the inner list, the second picks the element inside it.
question_patterns: Which single statement fetches the fifth subject's marks from stRecord?
Verify that the stored percentage 78.8 equals the total of the five marks divided by five.
How would you change the student's name from Raman to Raghav in the record?
What does stRecord[2][1] return for the given record?
Write a statement that stores the maximum of the five marks in a variable.

solution_steps.explain: Add every mark stored in the nested list.
Five subjects give the percentage 78.8 stored in the record.

worked_examples.q: In the record ['Ria', 'A-1', [56, 98, 99], 78.8], which first index picks the marks list?

concepts.title: Alias versus Clone of a List
concepts.definition: Assigning list2 = list1 only binds a second name to the same list object, so changes through either name show up in both; a genuine independent copy needs slicing with [:], the list() constructor, or copy.copy().
concepts.formula: clone = old_list[:] or list(old_list) or copy.copy(old_list)
concepts.key_idea: After appending 10 through list1, the alias list2 also shows 10, while a clone still holds the old contents.
question_patterns: After list2 = list1 and list1.append(10), why does printing list2 also show the appended 10?
Name the three ways of producing an independent copy of a list.
How does oldList[:] differ from oldList as the right side of an assignment?
A clone was made before the original was sorted. Does sorting the original disturb the clone?
What is an alias in the context of list assignment?

solution_steps.explain: Plain assignment shares one object id between both names; the three cloning routes create a new object whose later edits stay private.

worked_examples.q: Does the statement list2 = list1 create a clone or an alias?

concepts.title: Insert, Remove and Pop Shifting
concepts.definition: Because a list is mutable and ordered, insert() pushes later elements one place right, remove() deletes only the first match of a value, and pop() extracts the element at a given index (or the last one) while shrinking the list.
concepts.formula: new_len = old_len - 1 after one pop or remove
concepts.key_idea: Every insertion or deletion shifts the positions of the elements after the affected index.
question_patterns: After list1.insert(2, 25) on [10, 20, 30, 40, 50], where does 25 sit and where does 30 move?
For [10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60], what does pop(3) return and what remains in the list?
Why does remove(30) on [10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 30] leave one 30 behind?
How many elements remain after one pop() with no argument, and which element left?
Which exception appears when index() or remove() cannot find the requested element?

solution_steps.explain: Insertion at index k moves every element from k onwards one place right; deletion at k moves them one place left, and pop returns the removed element.

worked_examples.q: Which list method inserts an element at a chosen index, shifting later elements right?
